title: Proactive regression prober: SLO-aware PR gating with synthesized workload slices
creator: Priya Gupta
description: Objective: Build a CI-side prober that synthesizes representative workload slices from historical traces and evaluates PR changes with a probabilistic SLO-aware detector. The prober will be used as a gating step for pull requests that modify the serving runtime, kernel selection paths, batching logic, or KV cache behavior. Background: Existing CI gating relies on end-to-end baseline runs against a fixed synthetic load. We repeatedly see noisy p95 measurements and brittle pass/fail outcomes when upstream noise or small workload shifts occur. This results in developer friction (flaky gating) and occasional merged regressions. Proposal summary: 1) Synthesize workload slices: automatically extract representative request sequences from production traces (short and long sequences, high-length tails, conversational prefixes) and generate small, deterministic microbenchmarks that cover those slices. 2) Contextual sampling: choose 3–5 representative slices per PR based on changed code areas and historical hit rates. 3) Ensemble measurement: run a fast ensemble of probes per slice (lightweight synthetic runner + short shadowing against staging) to capture tokens/sec and p95 tail behavior. 4) Probabilistic detector: use a Bayesian hierarchical model (or bootstrapped nonparametric alternative) to detect regressions with uncertainty estimates and false-positive control (target alpha=0.01). 5) Gating policy: implement a soft-gate first (annotation + link) and escalate to hard-block if the detector reports a regression >= 7% on p95 tokens/sec with probability > 95% across 3 consecutive CI runs. Scope: implement probe harness, slice synthesizer, detector integration, CI job templates, dashboarding for probe runs, and PR annotation logic. Out of scope: full production shadowing, long-running soak tests, and detailed per-customer slicing in initial rollout.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic slice synthesizer exists that converts production trace windows into reproducible microbenchmarks
CI job template executes the prober within 12 minutes on a standard CI runner and reports tokens/sec and p95 per-slice
The detector issues quantitative probability of regression with a human-readable rationale and link to raw runs
PR gating respects the soft->hard escalation policy documented in the gating spec
Dashboard page displays last 30 probe runs, slice labels, and trend lines for p50/p95/tokens-per-sec
tasks: Design slice schema and extractor (trace window length, prefix retention, stochastic variation seeds)
Implement microbenchmark runner harness with configurable sequence injection and KV cache warmup
Integrate lightweight shadow runner for short-stage comparison against staging deployment
Develop probabilistic regression detector library and unit tests
Add CI job templates and PR annotation integration (GitHub Actions)
Create dashboard panels in Grafana/Chronograf and RBAC for internal teams
Document gating policy and runbook for triage of noisy failures
comments: 2025-02-11 - Priya Gupta: Spike done—extracted 12 candidate slices from last 7 days of traces; initial microbenchmarks run locally. Noted that long-conversation slices need explicit KV-warmup to avoid cold-start noise.
2025-02-13 - Ethan Park: Implemented prototype harness. With deterministic seeds, repeated runs reduce within-slice variance to ~2.1% p95 on our local devboard. Will instrument shadow runner next.

2025-02-15 - Maya Chen (SRE): Suggested adding system-level metrics (GPU utilization, PCIe stalls) to correlate with p95 spikes; also recommended storing raw trace snippets in object storage for reproducibility.

2025-02-17 - Priya Gupta: Detector design chosen: hierarchical Bayesian with student-t observation model to handle heavy tails. Fallback bootstrapped percentile test will be implemented for faster CI runs.
2025-02-18 - Product (Liam O'Connor): Approved P1 priority; requested clear UX for soft annotations in PRs and an option to ignore probe failures for low-risk docs changes.
implementation_notes: Keep each synthesized slice small (<= 60s wall time) so total job fits CI budget. Use stratified sampling to include tail cases at a higher rate than frequency in traces. Provide toggles to opt a PR into 'fast mode' (fewer slices) vs 'full mode' for larger changes.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: False positives due to infra noise. Mitigation: require repeated evidence across runs and include system metrics for triage. Risk: Overfitting probes to historical traces. Mitigation: rotate slice sets monthly and include randomized seed perturbations.
notes_for_reviewers: Focus reviews on detector assumptions and the tradeoff between detection sensitivity and developer friction. Review the proposed escalation thresholds and CI runtime budget. Feedback on alternative statistical tests (e.g., sequential probability ratio test) welcome.
